title: The fire made cool
hook: they throw Ibrahim into a great fire and Allah says, fire, be cool and safe for him (21:68–69)

segments.voice: Yesterday: ask them, if they can speak. The town admitted it. Your line was they cannot speak. What did you take the power back from? Day thirty-five.

Look back at this week. Nuh, calling for nine hundred and fifty years. Building a ship on dry land while people laughed. Calling to his son as the wave came between them. Then Ibrahim, watching the star set. Breaking the idols. Letting the town hear itself say: they cannot speak. And every one of those people paid for speaking up. Nuh was mocked. Ibrahim is about to find out what it costs. Because when a crowd is embarrassed in front of itself, it doesn't always change its mind. Sometimes it gets angry. And this crowd builds a fire.
screen: `A WEEK OF SPEAKING UP.` → `A CROWD, EMBARRASSED.` → `AND THEY BUILD A FIRE.`

segments.voice: Surah twenty-one. The crowd has lost the argument, so they reach for the only thing left. In Pickthall's words: “Burn him and stand by your gods, if ye will be doing.” The commentators' retellings make the fire enormous: people gathering wood for days, a blaze so hot that birds flying over it fell, and Ibrahim thrown in from a distance by a kind of catapult. Those details are tradition, and the Qur'an doesn't give them. What the Qur'an gives is one sentence, and it's God speaking to the fire itself: “O fire, be coolness and peace for Abraham.” In Arabic, bardan wa salaman. Cool, and safe. And the fire obeys. There's an old observation from the commentators that people love. If God had said only be cool, the fire might have frozen him. So He said cool, and safe. Exactly enough. Not too much. What was Ibrahim doing while he fell? A report in Bukhari, from Ibn Abbas, says his words as he was thrown into the fire were: hasbuna llahu wa ni'ma l-wakil. God is enough for us, and the best one to trust. The same words, the report says, were later said by the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his companions when they were told an army was gathering against them. It's a line Muslims still say when they're afraid. And notice the order. Ibrahim didn't wait to see whether the fire would cool before he trusted. The trust came first, in midair. The coolness came after. The fire didn't go out. It just couldn't touch him.
screen: `BURN HIM, AND STAND BY YOUR GODS.` · `O FIRE, BE COOL AND SAFE.` · `NOT ONLY COOL. SAFE.` · `GOD IS ENOUGH FOR US.` · then, large: `COOLNESS AND PEACE.`

segments.voice: The bell will give you two minutes. Think of something that feels like a fire right now. A deadline, a conflict, a fear that's been burning in the background. Let yourself feel the heat of it for a moment. Then breathe out slowly, all the way, three times. Long, cool breaths, like wind across the flames. After the third, just rest, and let the breath be easy. If you pray, you can hold Ibrahim's words: God is enough for us. The bell holds the time.
The fire made cool. Bardan wa salaman: God tells the fire to be cool and safe for Ibrahim, and it is.
Your line: cool and safe. Today, when something flares up, before you answer, breathe out slowly three times. Let it be cool, and safe. A week, done. Day thirty-five.

howItsDone: Many Muslims say hasbuna llahu wa ni'ma l-wakil, God is enough for us and the best one to trust, in moments of fear, remembering Ibrahim in the fire.

original.note: Arabic: "coolness and peace," what God tells the fire to be for Ibrahim (21:69).

trapdoor: what you thought: God put out the fire.
what it means: the fire made cool — the fire still burned, but God told it to be cool and safe for Ibrahim, and it couldn't harm him.

what a scholar hears: bardan wa salaman, cool and safe, which commentators say was said so the cold wouldn't harm him either; the wood, the birds and the catapult are tafsir; hasbuna llah is in Bukhari 4563.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 4563 (hasbuna llahu wa ni'ma l-wakil; 3:173)
al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir on 21:68–69 (the size of the fire; the catapult; 'cool and safe')

notes: The fire's size, the falling birds and the catapult (manjaniq) are from tafsir; the script says so plainly.
'If He had said only cool, it would have harmed him': reported from Ibn 'Abbas (and 'Ali) in tafsir. Stated as 'an old observation from the commentators'. Confirm.
Bukhari 4563: Ibn 'Abbas said hasbuna llahu wa ni'ma l-wakil was said by Ibrahim when thrown into the fire and by Muhammad ﷺ when told the people had gathered (3:173). Confirm.
Week-end look back is in the hook (days 29–34: Nuh and the first Ibrahim days).
